title: Gate automated response with approvals and stop controls / Capture automated-response audit evidence

steps.title: Gate automated response with approvals and stop controls

blocks.text: An aws:approve Automation step pauses for the designated approvers to approve or reject. Place it before the protected operation; a pending request is not approval.

Use the supplied branching or failure path to prevent the protected operation on rejection or stop. When a stop condition occurs, use the approved stop operation and inspect execution state before allowing further actions.

blocks.alt_text: Make the approval step's position before the protected operation visible, together with pending, rejected, and stopped execution states and the protected operation remaining unexecuted in each case.

steps.lede: Read the supplied excerpts in this step and decide which conclusions or actions are correct, defective or unsafe.

public.prompt: A stop condition occurs in an Automation response. What must happen before any further action is allowed?

options.text: Request the approved stop operation and inspect execution state before allowing further actions.
Request stop and immediately allow the protected operation without inspecting state.
Ignore the stop condition because an approval step exists in the workflow.

a.message: Correct. Request the approved stop operation and inspect execution state before allowing further actions.

b.message: A stop request alone does not replace inspecting execution state.

c.message: The approval step does not nullify a stop condition.

correct.message: Correct. Your judgement follows the supplied evidence and the stated requirement.

incorrect.message: Compare the evidence with the requirement rather than inferring success from a partial signal. The workflow pauses for designated approvers before the protected operation. Pending approval, rejection, and stop do not permit that operation. After requesting a stop, execution state is inspected before any further action is allowed.

hints: Separate the observed outcome from what was merely intended.
Check every required condition, not just the most reassuring field.

public.prompt: Read each approval/stop excerpt. Decide whether the protected operation is correctly blocked, or whether the alternate path improperly allows it.

items.text:
aws:approve precedes the protected operation and waits for designated approvers. Rejection follows the supplied blocking path. In the stopped case, the approved stop operation was requested and execution state inspected before considering further action.
```text
execution_id: "approval-pending"
approval_step: "aws:approve"
execution_state: "pending"
protected_operation_executed: false
```

aws:approve precedes the protected operation and waits for designated approvers. Rejection follows the supplied blocking path. In the stopped case, the approved stop operation was requested and execution state inspected before considering further action.
```text
execution_id: "approval-rejected"
approval_step: "aws:approve"
execution_state: "rejected"
protected_operation_executed: false
```

aws:approve precedes the protected operation and waits for designated approvers. Rejection follows the supplied blocking path. In the stopped case, the approved stop operation was requested and execution state inspected before considering further action.
```text
execution_id: "approval-stopped"
approval_step: "aws:approve"
execution_state: "stopped"
protected_operation_executed: false
```
Alternate excerpt: execution_state: pending; protected operation begins while designated approvers have not decided.
Alternate excerpt: stop condition occurs; stop is requested; protected operation proceeds without execution-state inspection.

steps.lede: Read the supplied excerpts in this step and decide which conclusions or actions are correct, defective or unsafe.

public.prompt: Which response record accurately represents both successful and failed actions?

options.text: Execution details retain inputs, outputs and failure information; underlying actions are linked to CloudTrail request identity and operation evidence.
Record only successful steps because failed steps have no useful evidence.
Treat the intended workflow plan as proof that its AWS actions occurred.

a.message: Correct. Execution details retain inputs, outputs and failure information; underlying actions are linked to CloudTrail request identity and operation evidence.

b.message: Failure information and failed outcomes belong in the response record.

c.message: Actual request identity and operation evidence, not intention, attribute underlying actions.

correct.message: Correct. Your judgement follows the supplied evidence and the stated requirement.

incorrect.message: Compare the evidence with the requirement rather than inferring success from a partial signal. The completed response record accurately captures the supplied execution identifiers, authority, targets, times and step details, links underlying actions to CloudTrail evidence, and retains both successful and failed outcomes without inferring actions from the intended plan.

hints: Separate the observed outcome from what was merely intended.
Check every required condition, not just the most reassuring field.

public.intro:
Read the supplied completed response record. Select the evidence that belongs in an accurate audit of both outcomes; do not infer actions from the intended plan.

The tasks are grouped into two sections: “Successful step” and “Failed step.” In each section, select the entire step record first, preserving its execution, authority, target, times, inputs, outputs and failure details. Then select each named evidence cell from that same step record.

Select the entire step record.
Request identity attributing the underlying action.

### Failed step
Select the entire step record.
Request identity attributing the underlying action.

blocks.text: Approval precedes the protected operation. Rejection or stop prevents it; inspect execution state after stopping.
Keep execution identity, role, targets, timing and complete step evidence. Attribute AWS actions with CloudTrail; retain failures too.
